prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The API now needs a key. No key or an unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized`, and a known key without permission gets 403 `forbidden`, both in the usual error shape. `viewer` keys can only read. `cook` keys can also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts; starting or finishing a stock-take is for managers. `manager` keys can do everything, and only they can read `GET /audit`, which lists newest first. Every non-GET request made with a known key gets an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status), even if it was refused or failed; requests refused with 401 are not logged. Storing keys and the audit log is a schema change, so the data is now schema 3 and older files open with no keys. That means an old data file refuses every request until keys are added to it. I put the same three keys in `data/db.json` as in `data/seed.json` so the local server still works. In the tests, requests now send the manager key unless a test sets its own headers. I added `tests/auth.test.js` and changed the migrate test in `tests/cli.test.js`, which hard-coded schema 2. `npm test` (31 tests) and `npm run lint` both pass.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
